drivingQuestion: What is the measure of כדי ביקור by which Rabbi Shimon disqualifies an interrupted slaughter?
outcomeNote: The אלא settles the measure as the examination performed by a slaughterer who is himself a Sage, so that the shiur does not vary with circumstance.

segments.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם שָׁהָה [כְּדֵי בִיקּוּר]. מַאי כְּדֵי בִיקּוּר? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּדֵי בִּיקֻּרוֹ שֶׁל חָכָם. אִם כֵּן, נָתַתָּ דְּבָרֶיךָ לְשִׁיעוּרִין! אֶלָּא, כְּדֵי בִּיקּוּר טַבָּח חָכָם.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Shimon says:» The slaughter is not valid «if he interrupted» the slaughter for an interval equivalent to the duration of an examination. The Gemara asks: «What» is an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination? Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» It is an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination» of the knife «by a Sage» prior to the slaughter of the animal. The Gemara objects: «If so, you have rendered your statement» subject «to circumstances,» as sometimes the Sage is near and sometimes the Sage is far, and the time required for examination varies accordingly. The Gemara responds: «Rather,» the reference is to an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination» performed by «a slaughterer» who is «a Sage.» In that case, travel time is not factored in; only the time of the examination itself is considered, and this does not vary.
